name: Product Attachments Test Relative Peeling
statement: Fix a finite ample family $R\subseteq Q_F$ containing $0_F$ that peels but has no peeling ending at $0_F$. For nonempty ample $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$, set $P_R(A,K)=(A\times\{0_F\})\cup(K\times R)$. Then $P_R(A,K)$ is ample, has $|A|+(|R|-1)|K|$ vertices, and peels if and only if $K$ peels and $A$ peels down to $K$. A fixed 289-vertex choice of $R$ therefore reduces relative peeling to ordinary peeling with constant-factor growth.
proof: If a shattered support uses a new coordinate, its old part is shattered by $K$ and its new part by $R$, so the product of witnessing cubes lies in $K\times R$; supports using only old coordinates are witnessed in $A$. For necessity, every root $(k,0)$ must retain a private neighbor when deleted, or the induced peeling of $R$ could end at its root. The missing mixed square then prevents a simultaneous neighbor in $A\setminus K$, and retaining all of $K$ yields a relative peeling of $A$; a nonroot layer restricts to a peeling of $K$. Conversely, peel $A$ to $K$ and then peel the product $K\times R$ layer by layer.
